items.title: Can We Recreate Sage2's Real-Time AI Extraction in Databricks? | System One Models Part 4
items.author: Advancing Analytics
items.summary:
Can you recreate real-time AI extraction in Databricks using AI Decide and System 1 models?

When Levanto released Sage2, a new approach to extracting structured information and making decisions from live conversations, we thought it looked pretty interesting.

So naturally, we wanted to see if we could build something similar in Databricks.

In this video, James and Bev experiment with real-time entity extraction using Databricks AI Extract, AI Decide and System 1 models. Inspired by Sage2's approach to extraction and streaming decisions, they explore how to capture information from live chat sessions, track changing customer intentions and make decisions as conversations unfold.

Along the way, they put different approaches to the test, digging into speed, accuracy, latency and cost to see what's possible with the tools available today.

In this video, you'll learn:
- What System 1 models are and how they enable fast, real-time information extraction.
- How Sage2 inspired the experiment, and what we're trying to recreate using Databricks.
- How to use Databricks AI Extract and AI Decide to extract structured information from live chat conversations.
- How to track changing customer intentions as new information becomes available.
- How different extraction approaches compare when it comes to speed, accuracy and latency.
- How to optimise extraction workflows to avoid unnecessary processing and reduce costs.
- Where real-time extraction could be useful, from customer service conversations to AI agents and document processing.

Who is this video for?

If you're a data engineer, AI developer or anyone experimenting with real-time AI applications, this one's for you.

Whether you're building AI agents, working with unstructured data or exploring how to extract information from live conversations, James and Bev take a practical look at what's possible using Databricks and System 1 models.
